title: Campaign: non-invasive brain measurement, fields and emissions produced by the brain itself
abstract: Subcampaign of 'how can human brain activity be measured without surgery, better than today?'. Scope: Methods that detect signals the brain generates, with no probing energy: EEG, MEG and optically pumped magnetometers, electrode placement, conduction-model calibration, and passive emissions (ultraweak photons, microwave and thermal noise). 91 papers. Status: bounds and narrow gains. Electrode position matters more than electrode type: in layered sphere models at equal electrode noise, only dense arrays in or below the bone sharpen EEG maps much (1.02-1.20 times smaller patches under the scalp, 2.3-5.0 times in bone or on the dura at 5 mm spacing); a 0.2 mm fluid film cuts a tight sheet's 7.2x sub-scalp gain to 3.1x; in recordings of known sources in 4 patients, a per-electrode correction halves the unexplained part of the scalp map (relative rms residual 0.21 to 0.11). Hippocampal ripples give 0.7-2 fT at the best MEG sensor, so MEG replay effects are possible only at the upper estimate. Many papers are exact-solution and identifiability checks of conduction models in spheres.
